page: Amazon Web Services x8g.24xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. The instance delivers 96 physical cores across 96 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is substantial at 1536 GB of RAM, establishing a high 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 16 GB allocated per core. Cache configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic operations benefit from hardware AES support, though standard x86 vector extensions are absent due to the ARM architecture. Networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 40 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no local instance storage bundled, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 163581.24, placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, while single-core performance registered in the middle 50 percent at 1706.59. The memory architecture achieved a top-tier small-block read bandwidth of 11084.58 GB/sec and an uncached 256 MB block read speed of 480.45 GB/sec, paired with 215.69 GB/sec write throughput. Geekbench scores reinforced this profile with a multi-core mark of 25694.0 and strong Clang software compilation throughput of 93482.0. In-memory data store performance proved notable, with Redis SET operations yielding 193.44 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 46856.13, both placing in the top decile. In CPU-based LLM inference, the system achieved top-tier text generation speeds across medium and large models.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the x8g.24xlarge stems from its high density of ARM cores and exceptionally large RAM allocation on a single virtual server. For organizations operating memory-bound workloads, Graviton-based architecture generally provides favorable compute-per-dollar efficiency compared to legacy x86 memory-heavy instances. However, workloads requiring local scratch space must absorb the cost and latency of remote EBS storage. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include distributed in-memory databases such as Redis or Memcached, large-scale SAP HANA deployments, relational databases, big data in-memory caching engines, and large-scale parallel software build systems.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.24xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and 64-bit ARM architecture. Equipped with 96 dedicated physical AWS Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 1536 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. The hardware incorporates 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, hardware AES encryption, and multi-tier caching, though it includes no local disk storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals top-tier multi-threaded compute capability and high memory bandwidth, highlighted by 193.44 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier multi-threaded decompression. Single-threaded metrics remain moderate. The architecture provides high resource density and operational cost efficiency for RAM-intensive tasks, making it suited for massive in-memory databases, real-time caching fleets, enterprise database hosting, and high-throughput memory-resident data analytics.

tagline: Massive memory density with ninety-six dedicated ARM cores designed for enterprise-grade in-memory computing and high-throughput cache layers.
bullet_points: 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.8 GHz with single-threaded execution
1536 GB system memory providing 16 GB of RAM per dedicated vCPU
40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth running on the AWS Nitro System
Top-tier memory read throughput exceeding 11 TB/sec in cached operations
Absence of local NVMe storage, relying fully on external network block storage
Optimal fit for large Redis clusters, relational databases, and in-memory analytics
